lessons.title: Trace event, request, template, channel and delivery evidence
lessons.overview: Notification work should be reasoned about as a pipeline. An owning Craves service produces an event or internal request, Notification Service validates the caller and request key, persists notification/audit state, renders an approved template, selects an enabled channel adapter, records the delivery attempt and later exposes evidence of success or failure. In-app persistence and external provider acceptance are different stages, and phone authentication OTP remains outside this transactional-notification boundary.

steps.label: Identify the source event
steps.detail: Start with the business event and source service rather than with an email/SMS provider.

steps.label: Trace internal authorization
steps.detail: Follow the internal notification controller and service-authentication requirements.

steps.label: Trace persistence
steps.detail: Locate request key, recipient reference, inbox/audit record and attempt state.

steps.label: Trace rendering
steps.detail: Identify the template and variables that turn the event into channel-specific content.

steps.label: Trace the adapter
steps.detail: Follow only the configured channel provider and its normalized success/failure result.

steps.label: Separate evidence
steps.detail: Distinguish request recorded, provider accepted, delivered/read and any retry attempt.

lessons.example: An in-app notification can exist while an email attempt is pending or failed. Support should inspect each channel attempt instead of inferring email delivery from the inbox row.
lessons.lab: Trace one synthetic internal notification from source event to InternalNotificationController, persisted request, template, provider attempt and result. Mark which stage proves what.
lessons.pitfall: Do not route Firebase phone-OTP troubleshooting through the transactional notification inbox just because both involve messages.

questions.prompt: What does a persisted notification request prove?
questions.explanation: Provider acceptance and end delivery require separate evidence.

questions.prompt: Where does phone authentication OTP belong?
questions.explanation: Authentication OTP and transactional notifications have different ownership.

lessons.title: Add a notification type without coupling the source service to providers
lessons.overview: A new notification should begin with an approved business event and stable internal contract, not provider-specific payload code in the source service. Define an event/request key, recipient semantics, template variables and allowed channels; implement or update the template and Notification Service handling; keep provider mapping inside channel adapters; then add observability and retry behavior. Do not include sensitive customer data in logs, idempotency keys or Academy examples.

steps.label: Define the event
steps.detail: Name the source event, recipient type and stable fields needed to render the message.

steps.label: Define idempotency
steps.detail: Choose a request/event key so retries do not create uncontrolled duplicate notifications.

steps.label: Add template
steps.detail: Create approved content variables and keep presentation separate from the source service's domain transaction.

steps.label: Select channels
steps.detail: Use enabled channel adapters and preference rules rather than hard-coding a provider call in the producer.

steps.label: Record attempts
steps.detail: Persist normalized attempt outcome and provider correlation data needed for support.

steps.label: Expose safe status
steps.detail: Return or display only the delivery information the caller is authorized to see.

lessons.example: Order can emit an approved order-ready notification request containing the minimal event facts; Notification Service decides how to render and send it through configured channels.
lessons.lab: Design a fictional notification type with event key, minimal payload, template variables, channel choices, duplicate handling, attempt states and tests. Use fake recipients only.
lessons.pitfall: Putting an email-provider SDK directly into every business service creates duplicated secrets, retry logic and failure behavior.

questions.explanation: Central provider adapters keep source services independent from channel vendors.

questions.prompt: What should make a retried notification request safe?
questions.explanation: A stable request key allows the service to detect and control retries.

lessons.title: Test channel failures, privacy and replay-safe recovery
lessons.overview: Notification tests should include duplicate internal requests, template-variable errors, disabled channels, provider timeout, provider rejection and repeated recovery. Assertions must verify both customer-visible behavior and retained attempt evidence. Production release checks confirm provider configuration and templates without sending uncontrolled messages. Recovery begins with the original request key and failure reason; it must not rewrite the source business event or leak customer contact data into diagnostics.

steps.label: Test duplicates
steps.detail: Replay the same request key and verify the configured duplicate behavior.

steps.label: Test rendering errors
steps.detail: Remove or invalidate a required synthetic template variable and assert a controlled failure.

steps.label: Test provider failure
steps.detail: Simulate timeout/rejection and confirm attempt state remains diagnosable and retryable.

steps.label: Test privacy
steps.detail: Ensure logs and Academy-facing diagnostics do not expose message bodies, real emails, phone numbers or secrets.

steps.label: Smoke configuration
steps.detail: Verify enabled channels/templates and provider connectivity through the approved non-destructive method.

steps.label: Recover by request key
steps.detail: Retry the failed delivery path using original event correlation rather than recreating the business action.

lessons.example: If an approval email fails after chef approval, use the notification request and attempt evidence to recover the email; do not repeat the chef approval transaction.
lessons.lab: Build a fake-notification failure matrix for duplicate request, missing template variable, provider timeout, disabled channel and retry. Record expected request and attempt states.
lessons.pitfall: Copying full production message payloads into tickets or training material can turn an operational fix into a privacy incident.

options: Original request/event correlation and failure evidence
questions.explanation: Correlation preserves causality and prevents duplicate business actions.

questions.prompt: Which data should not appear in Academy diagnostics?
options: Real contact details and message bodies
questions.explanation: Training and diagnostics do not require customer message content or PII.
